title: MARPOL – Prevention of Pollution from Ships
description: Test your understanding of MARPOL, pollution-prevention equipment, operational controls, documentation and practical compliance onboard ships.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the scope of MARPOL?
options: It only regulates pollution caused by oil tanker accidents
It covers pollution from both routine ship operations and accidental incidents
It primarily regulates port construction and dredging activities
It applies only when a ship operates inside territorial waters
questions.explanation: MARPOL addresses pollution from routine ship operations as well as pollution resulting from accidents.

questions.question: A crew member is unsure whether plastic packaging may be discharged far from land. What is the correct general rule?
options: Plastics may be discharged when the vessel is outside a Special Area
Plastics may be discharged after being shredded
Disposal of plastics into the sea is prohibited
Plastics may be discharged when entered in the Garbage Record Book
questions.explanation: MARPOL Annex V prohibits the disposal of plastics into the sea regardless of the vessel's distance from land.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an Oil Record Book?
options: To document relevant oil-handling and machinery-space operations
To record fuel prices and bunker consumption
To list the vessel's approved lubricating oils
To document garbage delivered to reception facilities
questions.explanation: The Oil Record Book documents specified operations involving oil, oily mixtures and oil residues.

questions.question: Which shipboard activity is primarily regulated by MARPOL Annex IV?
options: The discharge and treatment of sewage
The carriage of chemicals in bulk
The disposal of cargo residues classified as garbage
The control of sulphur emissions from fuel oil
questions.explanation: MARPOL Annex IV contains regulations for the prevention of pollution by sewage from ships.

questions.question: Why are some sea areas designated as MARPOL Special Areas?
options: To prohibit all commercial navigation in environmentally sensitive waters
To apply additional pollution controls because of environmental conditions and sea traffic
To transfer enforcement responsibility from coastal States to classification societies
To allow ships to discharge waste under simplified procedures
questions.explanation: Special Areas require stricter pollution-prevention measures because of their oceanographical, ecological and traffic characteristics.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes MARPOL Annex II from Annex III?
options: Annex II covers sewage, while Annex III covers garbage
Annex II covers harmful substances in packages, while Annex III covers chemicals in bulk
Annex II covers noxious liquid substances in bulk, while Annex III covers harmful substances in packaged form
Annex II covers oil cargoes, while Annex III covers air emissions
questions.explanation: Annex II applies to noxious liquid substances carried in bulk. Annex III applies to harmful substances carried in packaged form.

questions.question: What is the primary function of oily-water filtering equipment used for machinery-space bilge water?
options: To separate oil from water before any permitted overboard discharge
To transfer sludge directly to the incinerator
To measure the sulphur content of fuel oil
To disinfect machinery-space wastewater
questions.explanation: Oil-filtering equipment treats oily bilge water so that any permitted discharge complies with Annex I requirements.

questions.question: A vessel is preparing to enter an Emission Control Area. Which action may be necessary when compliance is achieved through low-sulphur fuel?
options: Changing over to compliant fuel before entering the area
Emptying the sludge tank before crossing the boundary
Stopping all auxiliary engines inside the area
Transferring fuel oil into the ballast tanks
questions.explanation: When separate compliant fuel is used, the fuel changeover must be completed before the vessel enters the applicable Emission Control Area.

questions.question: Which document would normally be most relevant when verifying the disposal and handling of ship-generated garbage?
options: Cargo Record Book
Garbage Record Book
Oil Record Book Part II
International Air Pollution Prevention Certificate
questions.explanation: The Garbage Record Book records specified garbage handling, discharge, incineration and delivery operations.

questions.question: Why is delivery of waste to a port reception facility still recorded when no discharge into the sea occurred?
options: To demonstrate how the waste was managed and removed from the vessel
To calculate the vessel's summer deadweight
To transfer responsibility for all previous waste operations to the port
To replace the vessel's Garbage Management Plan
questions.explanation: Records provide traceability and evidence that regulated waste was handled through an approved disposal route.

questions.question: An engineer discovers that the oily-water separator's monitoring equipment is defective. The holding tank is nearly full. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Discharge slowly while visually checking the overboard outlet
Bypass the monitoring equipment because tank capacity is limited
Retain or transfer the waste and arrange an approved disposal or repair solution
Dilute the bilge water until no oil is visible
questions.explanation: A defective monitoring or filtering system must not be bypassed. The waste should be retained, transferred or delivered through an approved arrangement.

questions.question: A Port State Control officer finds recorded Oil Record Book entries that do not match sludge tank soundings and disposal receipts. What is the principal concern?
options: The vessel may have used an incorrect fuel grade
The records may not accurately account for the handling of oil residues
The vessel may have exceeded its permitted ballast capacity
The classification society may have used the wrong survey interval
questions.explanation: Inconsistent quantities may indicate inaccurate records, unexplained disposal or possible unlawful discharge of oil residues.

questions.question: A chemical tanker is cleaning a tank that previously contained a noxious liquid substance carried in bulk. Which source should primarily govern the residue-handling procedure?
options: The vessel's Garbage Management Plan under Annex V
The approved procedures applicable under Annex II
The engine-room Oil Record Book procedures
The fuel changeover procedure required under Annex VI
questions.explanation: Tank washing and residue handling for noxious liquid substances carried in bulk are controlled under Annex II and the vessel's approved procedures.

questions.question: A packaged cargo is identified as a marine pollutant. Which combination is most relevant to compliant carriage?
options: Tank stripping, cargo heating and an Oil Record Book entry
Suitable packaging, marking, documentation and stowage
Sewage treatment, sampling and discharge monitoring
Fuel changeover, bunker sampling and emission certification
questions.explanation: Annex III controls harmful substances in packaged form through requirements such as packaging, marking, documentation and stowage.

questions.question: Food waste has been mixed with plastic packaging. How should the mixture generally be treated for discharge purposes?
options: As food waste because it forms the majority of the mixture
According to the stricter requirement applicable to the plastic component
As sewage if the waste originated in the galley
As unrestricted waste after comminution
questions.explanation: When garbage categories are mixed, the more stringent discharge requirement generally governs. Plastics may not be discharged into the sea.

questions.question: A vessel changes from conventional fuel to compliant low-sulphur fuel shortly after crossing into an Emission Control Area. What is the main compliance issue?
options: The fuel changeover should have been completed before entering the area
Fuel changeover is only permitted while the vessel is alongside
The changeover should have been entered in the Garbage Record Book
The vessel must stop before changing fuel grades
questions.explanation: When low-sulphur fuel is used for compliance, the vessel must have completed the changeover before entry into the applicable area.

questions.question: A vessel has an approved exhaust-gas cleaning system and uses fuel with sulphur content above the normally applicable fuel limit. What must the vessel principally demonstrate?
options: That the equivalent compliance method is approved and operating as required
That the fuel was purchased outside an Emission Control Area
That the main engine is operated below its normal load
That the excess sulphur is entered in the Oil Record Book
questions.explanation: An approved equivalent method, such as an exhaust-gas cleaning system, must achieve the required emission-control performance and be operated correctly.

questions.question: A passenger ship operating in a sewage Special Area intends to discharge treated sewage. Which factor is especially important?
options: Whether an approved treatment plant meeting the applicable Special Area standard is operating
Whether all food waste has first been discharged
Whether the vessel is using low-sulphur fuel
Whether the sewage has been entered in the Oil Record Book
questions.explanation: Passenger-ship sewage discharge in a designated Special Area is generally restricted unless an approved treatment plant meeting the applicable requirements is operating.

questions.question: An accidental oil spill occurs during bunkering. Why can MARPOL remain relevant even though the discharge was not intentional?
options: MARPOL only applies after the coastal State proves negligence
MARPOL covers both operational and accidental pollution from ships
MARPOL applies only when the spilled oil enters a Special Area
MARPOL automatically transfers liability to the bunker supplier
questions.explanation: The Convention addresses prevention and control of pollution arising from both normal operations and accidental events.

questions.question: During an onboard audit, garbage is correctly segregated but several disposal entries are missing. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Correct segregation removes the need for recordkeeping
The vessel may still be non-compliant because operational controls and records are separate requirements
Only the port reception facility is responsible for the missing entries
Entries are only required for plastics and no other garbage categories
questions.explanation: Physical waste handling and accurate recordkeeping are both important. Correct segregation does not excuse missing required records.
